tool_summary: Installs, upgrades, and removes Python packages. Can execute arbitrary setup.py/pyproject.toml build code and fetch packages from arbitrary index URLs.
platform_notes: pip3 behavior and flags are identical to pip; this is a sibling file required because posix_parser.cr resolves rulesets by exact binary name, and pip3 is invoked as a distinct binary on many systems.

rules.description: The -i/--index-url or --extra-index-url flags point pip at a package index other than the default PyPI. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar index is a common supply-chain attack vector, since the installed package's build scripts run with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but its install-time build scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installing directly from a VCS URL (git+, hg+, etc.) or a raw HTTP(S)/local path bypasses the package index entirely, fetching and executing code from a source that has not gone through any registry review.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but install-time build scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installs a package, which downloads it from an index and can execute arbitrary build code (setup.py, PEP 517 build backends) with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be uninstalled, but install-time build scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages Python packages. Read-only subcommands (list, show, search, freeze) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future pip3 subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
